payload.description_html: SAM-PK-K7710, six articulated skeletons of the Upper Permian neodiapsid Scyllacerta creanae, preserved in life position, huddled head to tail in an underground burrow. Because they are all of the same age, it is assumed that they are a hibernating brood. The fossil comes from the farm Leeukloof 43 in the Western Cape province, from beds of the Teekloof Formation (Endothiodon assemblage zone, Wuchiapingian).[1]
